questions.q: What are the three components that constitute the 'Acquisition Cost' of a fixed asset for depreciation calculation purposes?
questions.a: Acquisition Cost = Purchase Price + Installation Expenses + Pre-operating Expenses. A wrong answer (e.g., omitting installation or pre-operative costs) reveals the student treats 'cost' as only the invoice price, ignoring AS-10/Ind AS 16 principle that all costs necessary to bring the asset to working condition must be capitalised. This error propagates into understated depreciation and overstated profits.

questions.q: Explain why the SLN function in Excel requires an absolute reference for the salvage value cell but a relative reference for the asset cost cell when the formula is copied down a column of multiple assets.
questions.a: Salvage value and useful life are policy constants (same for all assets of a class), so they must be locked with $ (e.g., $H$5) to prevent shifting when copied. Asset cost varies per row, so it uses relative reference (e.g., G5) to pick up each asset's unique cost. A student who uses relative for salvage will get wrong depreciation for rows 2+ as the formula pulls empty/incorrect cells — this is the #1 spreadsheet error in board practical exams.

questions.q: A machine was purchased on 15-Oct-2022 for ₹8,00,000 with ₹50,000 installation. Salvage value is ₹50,000, useful life 8 years. Using SLM, compute the depreciation for FY 2022-23 (ending 31-Mar-2023) assuming the company follows the 'half-year convention' for assets installed after 30-Sep.
questions.a: Step 1: Acquisition Cost = 8,00,000 + 50,000 = ₹8,50,000. Step 2: Depreciable Amount = 8,50,000 - 50,000 = ₹8,00,000. Step 3: Annual SLM Depreciation = 8,00,000 / 8 = ₹1,00,000. Step 4: Half-year convention → 6 months depreciation = 1,00,000 × 6/12 = ₹50,000. A wrong answer (₹1,00,000) shows the student ignored the installation date and pro-rata rule — a frequent board exam trap where 'date of installation' in column C triggers the IF(MONTH>3) logic in the WDV period column.

questions.q: Compare the depreciation expense pattern over 5 years for an asset costing ₹10,00,000 (salvage ₹1,00,000, life 5 years) under SLM vs WDV. Which method front-loads expense and why does this matter for tax planning?
questions.a: SLM: ₹1,80,000 each year (constant). WDV: Year 1 ~₹3,72,000, Year 2 ~₹2,33,000, Year 3 ~₹1,46,000, Year 4 ~₹91,000, Year 5 ~₹57,000 (declining). WDV front-loads expense because it applies a fixed rate to a reducing base. This matters for tax: higher early depreciation → lower taxable profit → deferred tax liability. A student who says 'SLM front-loads' confuses the methods; one who cannot explain 'why' lacks conceptual link to time value of money (cross-subject: finance).

questions.q: A company's fixed asset schedule shows: Opening Gross Block ₹50,00,000, Additions ₹12,00,000, Deductions ₹3,00,000. Opening Accumulated Depreciation ₹18,00,000, Depreciation for year ₹6,50,000, Deductions from Depreciation ₹1,20,000. Compute Closing Net Block and identify which figure comes from the depreciation computation spreadsheet (Figure 3.8) vs. which is manually entered.
questions.a: Closing Gross Block = 50,00,000 + 12,00,000 - 3,00,000 = ₹59,00,000. Closing Accumulated Depreciation = 18,00,000 + 6,50,000 - 1,20,000 = ₹23,30,000. Closing Net Block = 59,00,000 - 23,30,000 = ₹35,70,000. The ₹6,50,000 (current year depreciation) is transferred FROM the DB/SLN computation spreadsheet (column M/K) — it is NOT manually entered. A student who enters it manually breaks the audit trail; board practical marking deducts marks for missing 'linkage' between computation sheet and schedule.

questions.q: Design a spreadsheet template for a new asset category 'Solar Power Plant' (useful life 25 years, SLM rate 3.17% per Companies Act). The template must handle: (a) mid-year installation with pro-rata depreciation, (b) automatic flag if salvage value > 5% of acquisition cost (violates Schedule XIV), (c) dynamic update when asset life is revised mid-life. List the key columns, formulas, and validation rules.
questions.a: Key columns: Asset ID, Name, Purchase Date, Install Date, Purchase Cost, Install Exp, Pre-op Exp, Acquisition Cost (formula: sum), Salvage Value (input + validation: <=5% of Acquisition Cost), Life (input), Method (SLM/WDV), Depreciation Start Year (IF install month>3 then Year+1 else Year), Annual Depreciation (SLN with absolute salvage/life), Accumulated Depreciation (running sum), Net Book Value (Acquisition - Accumulated). Validation: Data Validation on Salvage Value cell with custom formula =H5<=0.05*G5. For life revision: add 'Revised Life' column, use IF(Revised<>"", Revised, Life) in SLN. A poor answer misses pro-rata logic or validation — showing inability to translate regulatory rules into spreadsheet controls.
